the_reference.file: data/mods/gen3/moves.ts:526-547 (the gen3 override), which ends at line 546 in this.actions.useMove
the_reference.CORRECTION: This report previously said 'there is no sleeptalk override in data/mods/gen3/moves.ts, so base applies'. THAT IS FALSE -- gen3 DOES override sleeptalk.onHit (it filters the callee set by nosleeptalk/charge and emits |cant|...|nopp|). The conclusion survives only because the override also ends in this.actions.useMove. For a report whose declared method is source comparison, a false premise about the exact file it cites is the error that matters most, and it was caught by review rather than by me.
the_reference.behaviour: the gen3 override filters the callee set and then runs the chosen move through this.actions.useMove, which reaches the ordinary damage pipeline and the normal crit roll. gen3 crit rate is 1/16 (sim/battle-actions.ts:1629-1646, gen<=5 branch, critMult[1]=16). Nothing about a CALLED move suppresses crits -- only willCrit and the CriticalHit event, which the engine already models.

the_engine.behaviour: for each callee it calls generate_instructions_from_move(..., false) -- the 7th parameter is branch_on_damage, hardcoded false. With branch_on_damage false the damage block at ~2830 takes its final `else { regular_damage = avg_damage_dealt }`, which emits NO crit arm. Both the Case A (straddling KO) and Case B (non-lethal crit) partitions are gated on branch_on_damage.
the_engine.consequence: a Sleep-Talk-called critical hit is REACHABLE IN THE SIMULATOR AND ABSENT FROM THE ENGINE'S SUPPORT.

worked_example.protocol: |move|p2a: Articuno|Sleep Talk -> |move|p2a: Articuno|Ice Beam|p1a: Seaking|[from] Sleep Talk, |-crit|, |-damage|p1a: Seaking|59/290
worked_example.arithmetic: 98 = 2 x 49; 46 is the 0.925 average of the non-crit roll. The crit arm at ~92 is simply not enumerated.

disposition.why_not_a_limit: this is precisely the fidelity objective's failure mode -- engine support must contain every reachable sim transition, and this transition is reachable and absent. It is not a branch-set-versus-sample artifact: the engine enumerates a branch set here and the crit member is missing from it.
disposition.why_not_a_matcher_fix: the matcher is correct to reject. There is no arm to match against.
disposition.the_fix: thread branch_on_damage through to the Sleep Talk recursive call instead of passing false.

1_reachable_engine_panic.what: the first version of this patch made tests/test_engine_search_no_panic.py fail -- PanicException 'Invalid rest_turns value: 64' -- killing the searcher. PanicException derives from BaseException, so engine_search.py's `except Exception` does not catch it.
1_reachable_engine_panic.cause: the 16-roll loop calls run_move 32 times without re-applying between calls, while run_move always reverses. 31 spurious reversals of a DecrementRestTurns drove rest_turns out of its 0..=3 domain. Latent on main because only an AWAKE attacker reaches that path and carries no DecrementRestTurns; Sleep Talk is the only way a SLEEPING Rest user gets there, so propagating branch_on_damage is what made it reachable.
1_reachable_engine_panic.fix: re-apply between iterations. Note the state arrives APPLIED here, unlike at extra_branches where a reversal has already happened -- my first attempt applied unconditionally and panicked the other way, rest_turns -1. Guarded with a needs_reapply flag so the first iteration does not re-apply.

2_stale_first_move.what: Sleep Talk callees inherit first_move=true from Choice::default() via get_sleep_talk_choices; handle_both_moves clears it only on the outer choice. With branch_on_damage propagated, a Sleep Talk used SECOND fired the 32-way enumeration against an already-resolved Flail/Reversal/Substitute.
2_stale_first_move.measured: 12 branches -> 144, and ~8x slower per call, for zero fidelity gain
